executive_summary.headline: Describe a building, get an energy model
executive_summary.body: An open-source server lets an AI assistant build and simulate whole-building energy models from plain-language prompts, turning days of specialist setup into minutes.

executive_summary.headline: Gemini 4 Argon finds new fusion-physics test cases
executive_summary.body: New counterexamples to a 1967 stellarator conjecture give simulation teams fresh benchmarks, and 10,000 scientists can use the top Antigravity tier free for six months.

executive_summary.headline: Open tools let any lab run autonomous-science experiments
executive_summary.body: Autonomous Science Bench, a public leaderboard, and a Department of Energy skills catalog give small groups a way to measure and reuse agent workflows.

executive_summary.headline: Frontier open weights now run on a desk
executive_summary.body: Muse Spark Open runs on two Mac Studios and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt fits in 24GB, so individuals can keep sensitive work local.

executive_summary.headline: EU standards and research guidelines get concrete
executive_summary.body: The first harmonised AI Act standard was published, and the European research guidelines now cover agentic AI, so providers and labs have clearer routes to compliance.

top_picks.title: Plain-language prompts now build and simulate whole-building energy models
top_picks.summary: A National Laboratory of the Rockies team released an open-source server that lets an AI assistant drive the EnergyPlus-based OpenStudio toolchain: describe a prototype office or school, add a lighting or HVAC upgrade, and get a validated simulation. The accompanying SoftwareX paper documents 197 tools and a benchmark across six language models; the researchers say tasks that took days now take minutes.
top_picks.author: National Laboratory of the Rockies
top_picks.enterprise_adaptation: Share with your lab: have the building-science or facilities group describe one existing building in two sentences, let the assistant draft the model, and compare its upgrade estimate against the group's last hand-built run within 30 days.
top_picks.why_it_matters: Energy modeling has needed specialist software skills; a prompt-driven front end puts it within reach of architects, small design firms, and school facility teams.

top_picks.title: Gemini 4 Argon finds new fusion-physics counterexamples and opens a free science tier
top_picks.summary: With a university collaborator, the model found a broader class of counterexamples to a 1967 conjecture about stellarator magnetic fields, giving fusion teams new test cases for simulation codes. The launch also reports a roughly 100x quantum-circuit improvement checked in Lean, and offers 10,000 scientists the top usage tier of Google Antigravity free for six months.
top_picks.author: Google
top_picks.enterprise_adaptation: Steal this idea: take a verified-answer problem from your own field, ask the model for counterexamples or edge cases, and add whatever it finds to your regression suite within 30 days.

top_picks.title: A vision-language model that reads crystal structures retrieves materials from plain-English property queries
top_picks.summary: MIT researchers paired 3D atomic structures with text in one model, published in Nature Communications. It outperformed text-only models, and its top picks for solid-state lithium-ion electrolytes included materials independently flagged as promising.
top_picks.author: MIT
top_picks.enterprise_adaptation: Steal this idea: write the three property constraints you would give a new materials student as one natural-language query and see how many of the retrieved structures your group has not yet screened.

top_picks.title: Autonomous Science Bench scores agents on full design-build-test-learn lab campaigns
top_picks.summary: The benchmark runs six budgeted campaigns across biology, chemistry, and materials with eight agent configurations over 144 trials. The best configuration succeeded in 67% of trials, and the hardest campaign was solved in 3 of 24; v0.1 campaigns, a lab runtime, and a public leaderboard are released.
top_picks.author: arXiv
top_picks.enterprise_adaptation: Steal this idea: run the open v0.1 campaign closest to your lab's work with your current agent setup and post the score as the baseline to beat in 30 days.

top_picks.title: HIP predicts molecular Hessians directly, 1 to 2 orders of magnitude faster
top_picks.summary: Hessian Interatomic Potentials use an equivariant graph neural network to output symmetric Hessians in one pass, validated on transition-state search, geometry optimization, zero-point energy, and vibrational analysis. The paper is open access with code and weights released.
top_picks.author: Nature Computational Science
top_picks.enterprise_adaptation: Steal this idea: swap HIP into one transition-state search your group already runs and compare wall-clock time and the vibrational frequencies against the current method.

top_picks.title: Europe's research guidelines now cover agentic AI and AI-assisted peer review
top_picks.summary: The European Commission published the fourth version of its living guidelines on generative AI in research. It adds guidance for agentic AI and more detail on AI in peer review and proposal evaluation; it applies to researchers, funders, and research organisations working with EU programmes.
top_picks.author: European Commission
top_picks.enterprise_adaptation: Steal this idea: use the agentic-AI section as a ready-made checklist for your lab's AI-use statement, and draft that one-page statement within 30 days.

sections.title: AI for Science
sections.description: Materials, chemistry, simulation, and autonomous discovery.

items.title: AI-Donkey turns first-principles GW workflows into runnable, repeatable agent tasks
items.summary: Out-of-the-box agents average 54%, 36%, and 19% on GW, GW-BSE, and GWPT workflow benchmarks. The AI-Donkey framework produces complete runnable workflows with no run-to-run variation, across proprietary and open-weight models.
items.author: arXiv
items.enterprise_adaptation: Steal this idea: encode one multi-step electronic-structure calculation your group repeats as a framework workflow and rerun it across two models to confirm identical results.

items.title: MAD-COSMO merges open datasets into a 1.7-billion-structure pool with a diverse coreset
items.summary: The work combines open structural datasets into about 1.7 billion structures and selects the 2^24 most diverse as a stratified coreset, giving small groups a manageable training set for atomistic models.
items.author: arXiv
items.enterprise_adaptation: Steal this idea: fine-tune a small interatomic model on the coreset for your element set and compare against your current training data.

items.title: The Agentic Scientist orchestrates coding agents for computational research alongside human researchers
items.summary: The pipeline splits research into task drafting, ideation, planning, sandboxed experiments, baselines and ablations, analysis, and report writing, with a meta-controller running parallel threads. A paper written with its co-scientist mode was accepted at ALIFE 2026.
items.author: arXiv
items.enterprise_adaptation: Steal this idea: hand the pipeline one open question from your backlog and review the baselines and ablations it builds before deciding what to run yourself.

items.title: AI plus symmetry searches woven sound-absorbing designs in under a minute
items.summary: An international team grouped weave patterns by four symmetry types, trained a predictor on a selected set of acoustic simulations, and then searched candidate designs in under a minute. Predictions matched independent detailed simulations within 5%, replacing hour-long simulations per design.
items.author: Tohoku University AIMR
items.enterprise_adaptation: Steal this idea: use symmetry classes to shrink any large pattern-design space your group explores, then train a quick surrogate on a few hundred simulations.

sections.title: Lab Adoption
sections.description: Programs, catalogs, and free access that labs can use now.

items.title: A public catalog of reusable agent skills is available for scientific workflows
items.summary: The Department of Energy released a public GitLab catalog of agent skills covering data governance, agent evaluation, and scientific workflows. Labs can adopt skills as published or adapt them to their own instruments and data.
items.author: U.S. Department of Energy
items.enterprise_adaptation: Steal this idea: pick the one skill closest to your daily analysis and install it in your lab's agent setup this month.

items.title: Eligible U.S. academic labs can get 30 free seats with GPT-Rosalind for 12 months
items.summary: The Rosalind Academic Plan gives approved PIs up to 30 Business Standard seats at $0 for up to 12 months, with GPT-Rosalind and Rosalind Workbench after trusted-access approval. Research data shared through the plan is not used for training by default; API access is not included.
items.author: OpenAI
items.enterprise_adaptation: Steal this idea: assign one life-science workflow, such as literature triage or protocol drafting, to each of the first five seats and compare time spent after a month.

items.title: Up to 200 European researchers get frontier science models and $3 million in compute credits
items.summary: Google DeepMind and Google Cloud will give selected researchers direct access to AlphaFold 3, WeatherNext, AlphaGenome, AlphaEvolve, and AlphaEarth Foundations, supporting the EU's RAISE initiative for AI in science.
items.author: Google DeepMind
items.enterprise_adaptation: Steal this idea: draft a one-page proposal naming one dataset and one model from the list, so your application is ready the day the call opens.

items.title: OpenGCUA releases a fully open stack for computer-use agents that write code as they work
items.summary: The first release opens the agent design, in which code execution lets intermediate results decide the next action, and proposes moving some harness decisions into the model. It gives indie builders an inspectable alternative to closed computer-use systems.
items.author: arXiv
items.enterprise_adaptation: Steal this idea: point the open stack at one repetitive desktop chore of your own and log where code execution beats clicking.

items.title: ATAS keeps long AI-generated films consistent across shots using scene and event memory
items.summary: The framework compiles a screenplay into shot requests with location, camera, and event-time references, retrieves scene and event memory before generating, and updates memory only after review. Across four video generators it improves every reported cross-shot consistency measure.
items.author: arXiv
items.enterprise_adaptation: Steal this idea: keep a simple shot list with fixed location and time tags for your next short film and feed it to your generator with every request.

items.title: Self-evolving harnesses let agents improve their own prompts, memory, and tools without retraining
items.summary: The paper formalizes how an agent's scaffolding can be revised across runs with model weights fixed, with a generalization bound and an admission rule that uses fresh validation data.
items.author: arXiv
items.enterprise_adaptation: Steal this idea: log failed runs from your own agent for one week and let it propose one revision to its prompt or tool list, then test the change on held-out tasks.

sections.title: Model Cards
sections.description: New open-weight and voice models, with the hardware they run on.

items.title: Muse Spark Open puts an 816B-parameter open-weight model on two desktop Mac Studios
items.summary: The natively multimodal model has 42B active parameters and a 1M-token context, and runs on two paired Apple M5 Ultra machines via MLX. Weights are on Hugging Face under the Muse Model License, which allows many developers to use it free; hosted access is available through seven inference partners.
items.author: Meta AI Research
items.enterprise_adaptation: Steal this idea: run the weights on local hardware for one private-data task you would never send to a hosted API.

items.title: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt fits a 74B-parameter agent model into 24GB at 80+ tokens per second
items.summary: Compressed from a 120B parent model with 2-bit expert quantization, the model targets everyday agentic tasks on RTX and DGX Spark machines. It ranks #1 on PinchBench, and #2 on WebArena and BrowseComp among models of similar memory footprint.
items.author: NVIDIA Research
items.enterprise_adaptation: Steal this idea: swap it in as the local browsing agent on a 24GB GPU and time a weekly research-gathering routine against your hosted setup.

items.title: GPT-Live-1.1 system card details a full-duplex voice model that handles interruptions
items.summary: GPT-Live-1.1 and its Quip variant listen and respond continuously, following pauses, interruptions, and changes in pace; 1.1 is the default voice model for Plus and higher tiers and Quip for others. The card reports voice-native evaluations.
items.author: OpenAI
items.enterprise_adaptation: Steal this idea: record a hands-free voice session for your next brainstorm and count how often interruptions land naturally.

items.title: NIST, NSA, and CISA publish ten voluntary practices for incidents during AI training and evaluation
items.summary: The voluntary document organizes ten practices across preparation, detection, response, recovery, and reporting, aimed at incidents where AI agents take significant uninstructed actions beyond the scope the operator set. It applies to frontier developers and anyone running agent evaluations.
items.author: NIST

items.title: The EU publishes its first harmonised standard for the AI Act, on AI quality management
items.summary: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2274, published 14 October, cites EN 18286:2026 for AI quality management systems. Providers who follow it get a presumption of conformity under Article 40, which makes the route to compliance concrete for small providers selling in the EU.
items.source: Official Journal of the European Union
items.author: European Commission

items.title: The UK AI Security Institute names eight priority areas for frontier AI technical practice
items.summary: The institute sets out the technical practices and controls it considers most urgent and how it will work with developers to shape best practice that could later inform formal standards. It states it is not seeking to mandate requirements.
items.author: UK AI Security Institute

emerging_signals.pattern: Domain tool servers and skill catalogs are becoming the way science agents get specialist abilities
emerging_signals.evidence: OpenStudio-MCP exposes 197 building-modeling tools, the Department of Energy released a public agent-skills catalog, and AI-Donkey packages GW workflows as repeatable tasks.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Whether more labs publish their own servers and skills for instruments and simulators.

emerging_signals.pattern: Sponsored frontier access for individual labs is expanding
emerging_signals.evidence: 30 free seats per approved U.S. lab, 10,000 free top-tier Antigravity scientist slots, and credits for up to 200 European researchers all opened within one week.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Application windows and eligibility rules for each program.

emerging_signals.pattern: Large open-weight models are moving to personal hardware
emerging_signals.evidence: Muse Spark Open runs on two Mac Studios and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt fits 74B parameters into 24GB.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Independent benchmark reproductions on consumer hardware.

emerging_signals.pattern: Voluntary US practices are taking shape ahead of binding rules
emerging_signals.evidence: NIST, NSA, and CISA published ten voluntary incident practices on 16 October; Colorado's interim ADMT and chatbot draft rules (released 6 October) go to hearing on 26 October, when comments close.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: The 26 October Colorado hearing and the task force's 120-day report clock.

flagged_unverified.claim: The White House Super Intelligence task force held its first meeting on 15 October and agreed to commission an advisory-council report on AI risk and to create an enforcement and consumer-protection committee.
flagged_unverified.reason: Reported by Semafor, Politico, and Reuters only; no whitehouse.gov primary document was found.

flagged_unverified.claim: The FTC issued civil investigative demands to two frontier AI developers on 14-15 October.
flagged_unverified.reason: Only secondary reports (Axios, CBS) were found; ftc.gov returned no matching release.

flagged_unverified.claim: A machine-learning map of about 10,000 CO2-to-fuel reaction steps on copper was presented as a new result.
flagged_unverified.reason: Press coverage appeared 13 October, but the Nature Communications paper was published 17 September, so it is excluded as not current-week.
